exports.description:
A server-safe IconButton with no tooltip: the same `<button>`, classes and CSS as `<IconButton tooltip={false}>`, from a module that imports no client code.

Use it only where visible text already names the action for sighted users (a column header, a labelled row) and the page should ship no JavaScript for the button: a table row action that is a link (`render={<a href="/orders/42/edit" />}`) under a header that says what it does, a submit button in a Server Action form (`type="submit"` inside `<form action={deleteProduct}>`) beside its label. Under Turbopack and `next dev`, importing `IconButton` ships its tooltip code even with `tooltip={false}` (about 20 KB gzip in production); `IconButtonStatic` ships none.

An icon-only toolbar needs `IconButton`'s tooltip, so a sighted user can read what each glyph does.

`aria-label` is always required. You may also pass `aria-labelledby` pointing at visible text; it then names the button, with `aria-label` as the fallback. There is no `tooltip`, no `shortcut` (pass `aria-keyshortcuts` yourself, for example `"Meta+B Control+B"`) and no `label`.
exports.name: IconButtonStatic
